title: All Roman doctors confess that the first man was not liable to death before sin
source_text: I. Primum hominem, antequam peccaret, non fuisse morti obnoxium; quemadmodum jam sumus omnes, sed aliquo sensu immortalem, res est apud omnes Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae confessa. Nam communi consensu tuentur adversus Pelagianos necessitatem moriendi, quae jam nobis incumbit, ex peccato ortum habuisse; nec fuisse locum habituram, si homo in primaeva illa integritate permansisset.
pass_a_gloss: That the first man, before he sinned, was not liable to death, as we all now are, but in some sense immortal, is a thing confessed among all the Doctors of the Roman Church. For by common consent they maintain against the Pelagians that the necessity of dying, which now lies upon us, had its origin from sin; and that it would have had no place, if man had remained in that primeval integrity.
pass_b_english: All the teachers of the Roman Church admit that the first man, before he sinned, was not subject to death as we all now are, but was in some sense immortal.
Against the Pelagians they hold by common consent that the necessity of dying which now lies on us arose from sin, and would have had no place if man had remained in his original integrity.

choices.why: The qualifier sets up the distinctions of the next theses; the English keeps it hedged.
